label: Darwall, p. 15: conceptual interdefinability does not show any second-personal authority exists
interpretation: Direct explicit concession: even if these concepts are irreducibly mutually linked, that does not entail any of their instances. This is not a claim that the concepts actually lack instances; it rejects treating their definitions as a proof of existence.
attribution: The passage states that mutual interdefinability of second-personal authority, valid demands, responsibility and reasons does not entail any actual instance, which is the no-existence-inference premise and not a claim that no moral authority exists.
